title: What's Hot in Seoul This Week? Your 2026 Salaryman Guide
keyword: what is hot in seoul this week
tldr: As of September 08, 2026, Seoul is buzzing with new AI profile picture trends, making everyone look like a K-drama star.
Convenience stores are seeing a massive boom in high-protein, ready-to-eat meals, perfect for the palli-palli (hurry-hurry) lifestyle.
Locals are flocking to 'healing' themed cafes and niche neighborhoods for unique, calming experiences away from the usual tourist traps.
target_audience: This is for readers who are curious about what's genuinely trending in Seoul right now and want an honest, insider perspective from a local.
content:
📅 Updated 2026.09.09
Key takeaways
  • As of September 08, 2026, Seoul is buzzing with new AI profile picture trends, making everyone look like a K-drama star.
  • Convenience stores are seeing a massive boom in high-protein, ready-to-eat meals, perfect for the palli-palli (hurry-hurry) lifestyle.
  • Locals are flocking to 'healing' themed cafes and niche neighborhoods for unique, calming experiences away from the usual tourist traps.
👤 This is for readers who are curious about what's genuinely trending in Seoul right now and want an honest, insider perspective from a local.

So, you're curious about what is hot in Seoul this week? Good. You've probably seen the flashy headlines, but let me tell you what's really happening on the ground, as of September 08, 2026. Forget the old stuff; right now, it's all about hyper-personalized digital experiences, health-conscious convenience, and finding quiet corners in a city that never stops.

The AI Profile Picture Boom: Everyone's a Star Now

Honestly, I thought this trend would fade, but it's just getting wilder. Remember those AI profile pictures from a year or two ago? Well, they've evolved. Now, the apps are so sophisticated, they can turn your ordinary selfie into something that looks like it belongs on a K-drama poster or a high-fashion magazine cover. My younger coworker, Kim, just did it last week using a new app called 'Facetune AI' (not its real name, but you get the idea), and suddenly he had a LinkedIn profile pic that looked like he'd just landed a modeling contract. He paid about ₩7,000 (roughly $5 USD) for a pack of 20 images. The algorithms are scary good at understanding current beauty standards and adapting your face to them. It’s a bit of a laugh in the office, but everyone’s doing it, even the department head's wife, apparently. It's the ultimate 'glow-up' without any actual effort.

Point: It's an accessible, affordable way for anyone to get a perfectly polished, on-trend digital persona without breaking the bank or hiring a photographer.

Protein Power-Ups: Our New Convenience Store Obsession

Look, we Koreans love our convenience stores. They're not just for snacks; they're lifelines. And lately, what is hot in Seoul this week at every GS25, CU, and 7-Eleven is anything high-protein. As a salaryman, I'm always looking for something quick and healthy, and these places have seriously stepped up their game. You used to just get ramen and 삼각김밥 (samgak kimbap, triangle gimbap). Now, you walk in and there are entire sections dedicated to high-protein chicken breasts, pre-packaged salads with protein toppings, protein drinks, even protein-fortified bread. I grab one of these chicken breast packs – usually ₩3,500 to ₩6,000 (around $2.50-$4.50) – for lunch at my office desk at least three times a week when I'm swamped. My company's cafeteria food is fine, but sometimes you just need something fast and guilt-free. It’s part of a wider health kick that's caught on, fueled by social media influencers showing off their gym routines and 'mukbang' (eating show) stars now promoting healthy options. It’s practical, it’s cheap, and it fits our busy lifestyle.

Point: Health-conscious convenience food is booming, and the local stores are making it easier than ever to grab a decent meal on the go.

The Rise of 'Healing' Cafes and Niche Neighborhood Journeys

Seoul is famous for its bustling cafes, but what is hot in Seoul this week isn't just about the prettiest latte art anymore. People, especially after a long week of work and the constant palli-palli (hurry-hurry) culture, are actively seeking out 'healing' spaces. These aren't necessarily quiet, meditative places, but rather cafes with a unique, often retro or nature-inspired theme that encourages slower living. Think LP (long-play record) listening cafes in Euljiro where you can actually pick out vinyl, or plant-filled greenhouses that serve as coffee shops in Ikseon-dong. My girlfriend dragged me to one of these 'forest-themed' cafes last weekend, tucked away in a tiny alley near Anguk Station. It was packed, but the vibe was so different – soft jazz, dim lighting, and everyone just quietly enjoying their drinks or reading. It's about finding these hidden gems in niche neighborhoods that haven't been fully gentrified or overrun by tourists yet. Using Naver Maps or Kakao Maps to scout out these specific, often tiny, spots is part of the adventure. It’s a rebellion against the mainstream, a search for authentic experiences where you can genuinely relax, even for an hour or two.

Point: Locals are trading flashy, Instagrammable spots for genuinely calming, uniquely themed 'healing' cafes in less explored parts of the city.

K-Resale Culture: Secondhand is the New New

Sustainability and unique finds are big right now, and the K-resale market is absolutely exploding. What is hot in Seoul this week in fashion and home goods is increasingly about finding pre-owned treasures. It's not just about vintage shops in Gwangjang Market anymore. It's largely driven by apps like 'Karrot Market' (당근마켓, Danggeun Market) or 'Bunjang' (번개장터, Bungae Jangteo), where people buy and sell everything from luxury handbags and limited-edition sneakers to used electronics and even furniture. My younger sister is obsessed with finding unique clothing pieces on these apps. She claims she snagged a nearly-new designer bag for half price last month. I actually sold an old gaming console on Karrot Market recently; it was surprisingly easy, and I got about ₩150,000 (around $110 USD) for it. These platforms are incredibly popular because they're convenient, often local (you can meet up with sellers in your neighborhood), and you can find things you won't see anywhere else. It’s a savvy way to save money, be eco-conscious, and still stay stylish or get the gadgets you want.

Point: Online resale platforms are now a go-to for finding unique items and embracing sustainable shopping, driven by convenience and value.

How to do it, step by step

  1. 1
    Step 1: Download the Right App for AI Profiles
    Search your app store for trending AI profile apps like 'Facetune AI' or 'Snow AI' (hypothetical names) – check Korean app store charts for the most popular ones as of September 2026.
  2. 2
    Step 2: Prepare Your Photos
    Upload 10-20 clear, varied selfies and full-body shots to the app; the more diverse your photos, the better the AI can learn your features.
  3. 3
    Step 3: Choose Your AI Style Pack
    Select from various styles (e.g., 'K-Drama Star', 'Professional CEO', 'Fantasy Warrior') and pay the fee, usually around ₩5,000-₩10,000 ($4-$8 USD).
  4. 4
    Step 4: Wait for AI Generation
    Wait typically 30 minutes to a few hours for the AI to process your images and generate a diverse set of new profile pictures.
  5. 5
    Step 5: Share and Update Your Profiles
    Pick your favorite AI-generated photos and update your social media, LinkedIn, or KakaoTalk profiles, joining the latest trend in Seoul.

Quick Q&A

Q. How much do these trending experiences typically cost in Seoul?

A. Trying the AI profile picture trend usually costs around ₩5,000-₩10,000 ($4-$8 USD) per pack. High-protein convenience store meals range from ₩3,500-₩6,000 ($2.50-$4.50 USD). A coffee or drink at a 'healing' cafe might be ₩5,000-₩8,000 ($4-$6 USD).

Q. Are these trends suitable for solo travelers visiting Seoul?

A. Absolutely. AI profile apps are a personal experience. Enjoying a high-protein meal from a convenience store is perfect for solo dining. Many 'healing' cafes are designed for quiet contemplation, making them ideal for solo visitors looking to unwind and enjoy a peaceful moment.

Q. Where can I find the most popular trending spots for 'healing' cafes in Seoul?

A. For 'healing' cafes, focus on exploring areas like Ikseon-dong, Euljiro, or even specific alleys in Seongsu-dong and Yeonnam-dong. Use local navigation apps like Naver Maps or Kakao Maps, searching for terms like 'LP cafe,' 'plant cafe,' or specific neighborhood names to discover hidden gems.

Q. How long do these trends usually last in Seoul before new ones emerge?

A. Seoul's trends can be quite dynamic due to the palli-palli (hurry-hurry) culture. While some, like the convenience store health trend, have deeper roots, specific fads like certain AI profile styles or themed cafes can shift every few months. It's best to check local social media or blogs like this one for the most current updates.

Q. Is it hard for foreigners to use Korean apps for these trends if they don't speak Korean?

A. Many popular apps, especially for services like AI profiles or online shopping, often offer English language options or have intuitive interfaces. For navigation, Naver Maps and Kakao Maps are highly visual. However, for local resale apps like Karrot Market, some basic Korean might be helpful for direct communication with sellers, though translation features are improving.

Sources I used

  • Korea Tourism Organization
  • Naver (for current trends & maps)

서울에서 이번 주에 인기 있는 것은 무엇일까요? 2026년 직장인을 위한 가이드

자, 이번 주 서울에서 무엇이 인기 있는지 궁금하시군요? 좋습니다. 화려한 헤드라인을 보셨겠지만, 2026년 9월 8일 현재 실제로 현장에서 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는지 말씀드리겠습니다. 옛날 것은 잊으세요. 지금은 초개인화된 디지털 경험, 건강을 생각하는 편리함, 그리고 결코 멈추지 않는 도시에서 조용한 구석을 찾는 것이 전부입니다.

## AI 프로필 사진 붐: 이제 모두가 스타

솔직히 이 트렌드는 시들해질 줄 알았는데, 점점 더 거세지고 있습니다. 1, 2년 전의 AI 프로필 사진을 기억하시나요? 글쎄요, 그것들이 진화했습니다. 이제 앱들은 너무 정교해서 평범한 셀카를 K-드라마 포스터나 하이패션 잡지 표지에 나올 법한 것으로 바꿔줍니다. 제 젊은 동료 김 씨는 지난주에 '페이스튠 AI'라는 새로운 앱(실제 이름은 아니지만 어떤 것인지 아실 겁니다)을 사용했는데, 갑자기 그가 모델 계약을 막 따낸 것처럼 보이는 링크드인 프로필 사진을 갖게 되었습니다. 그는 20장의 이미지 팩에 약 7,000원(약 5달러)을 지불했습니다. 알고리즘은 현재의 미의 기준을 이해하고 얼굴을 그에 맞게 조정하는 데 놀랍도록 뛰어납니다. 사무실에서는 좀 웃기지만, 부서장 부인까지도 다들 하고 있는 것 같습니다. 실제 노력 없이도 최고의 '글로우업'입니다.

> 요점: 누구나 큰돈을 들이거나 사진작가를 고용하지 않고도 완벽하게 다듬어진, 트렌디한 디지털 페르소나를 얻을 수 있는 접근성 좋고 저렴한 방법입니다.

## 단백질 파워업: 우리의 새로운 편의점 집착

보세요, 우리 한국인들은 편의점을 사랑합니다. 편의점은 간식만을 위한 곳이 아닙니다. 생명줄이죠. 그리고 요즘 GS25, CU, 7-Eleven에서 이번 주 서울에서 인기 있는 것은 고단백질 제품입니다. 직장인으로서 저는 항상 빠르고 건강한 것을 찾는데, 이 편의점들이 정말 수준을 높였습니다. 예전에는 라면과 삼각김밥만 살 수 있었죠. 이제 들어가 보면 고단백 닭가슴살, 단백질 토핑이 올라간 미리 포장된 샐러드, 단백질 음료, 심지어 단백질 강화 빵까지 전용 코너가 있습니다. 저는 바쁠 때 일주일에 최소 세 번은 이 닭가슴살 팩(보통 3,500원에서 6,000원, 약 2.50달러에서 4.50달러)을 사무실 책상에서 점심으로 먹습니다. 회사 구내식당 음식도 괜찮지만, 가끔은 빠르고 죄책감 없는 것이 필요합니다. 이는 소셜 미디어 인플루언서들이 운동 루틴을 자랑하고 '먹방' 스타들이 이제 건강한 옵션을 홍보하면서 확산된 더 넓은 건강 열풍의 일부입니다. 실용적이고, 저렴하며, 우리의 바쁜 생활 방식에 잘 맞습니다.

> 요점: 건강을 생각하는 간편식품이 급증하고 있으며, 지역 상점들은 이동 중에도 괜찮은 식사를 할 수 있도록 그 어느 때보다 쉽게 만들고 있습니다.

## '힐링' 카페와 틈새 동네 여행의 부상

서울은 번화한 카페로 유명하지만, 이번 주 서울에서 인기 있는 것은 더 이상 가장 예쁜 라떼 아트에 관한 것만이 아닙니다. 사람들은, 특히 긴 한 주간의 업무와 끊임없는 빨리빨리 문화 이후에, '힐링' 공간을 적극적으로 찾고 있습니다. 이것들은 반드시 조용하고 명상적인 장소라기보다는, 느린 삶을 장려하는 독특하고 종종 레트로하거나 자연에서 영감을 받은 테마를 가진 카페들입니다. 을지로에서 실제로 LP(롱플레이 레코드)를 고를 수 있는 LP 감상 카페나, 익선동에서 커피숍 역할을 하는 식물로 가득 찬 온실을 생각해 보세요. 지난 주말에 여자친구가 저를 안국역 근처의 작은 골목에 숨어 있는 이런 '숲 테마' 카페로 끌고 갔습니다. 붐볐지만 분위기는 너무 달랐습니다. 부드러운 재즈, 은은한 조명, 그리고 모두가 조용히 음료를 즐기거나 책을 읽고 있었습니다. 이것은 아직 완전히 젠트리피케이션되거나 관광객으로 넘쳐나지 않은 틈새 동네에서 이런 숨겨진 보석을 찾는 것에 관한 것입니다. 네이버 지도나 카카오 지도를 사용하여 이런 특정하고 종종 작은 장소들을 찾아내는 것이 모험의 일부입니다. 이것은 주류에 대한 반항이며, 한두 시간이라도 진정으로 휴식을 취할 수 있는 진정한 경험을 찾는 것입니다.

> 요점: 현지인들은 화려하고 인스타그램에 올릴 만한 장소 대신, 덜 알려진 도시 지역에서 진정으로 차분하고 독특한 테마의 '힐링' 카페를 찾고 있습니다.

## K-리셀 문화: 중고가 새로운 뉴

지속 가능성과 독특한 발견이 지금 큰 인기를 끌고 있으며, K-리셀 시장은 폭발적으로 성장하고 있습니다. 이번 주 서울에서 패션과 생활용품에서 인기 있는 것은 점점 더 중고 보물을 찾는 것에 관한 것입니다. 더 이상 광장시장의 빈티지 상점에 관한 것만이 아닙니다. 주로 '당근마켓'이나 '번개장터'와 같은 앱에 의해 주도되는데, 사람들은 명품 핸드백과 한정판 스니커즈부터 중고 전자제품, 심지어 가구까지 모든 것을 사고팝니다. 제 여동생은 이 앱들에서 독특한 의류를 찾는 데 집착합니다. 그녀는 지난달에 거의 새것 같은 디자이너 가방을 반값에 샀다고 주장합니다. 저는 실제로 최근에 당근마켓에서 오래된 게임 콘솔을 팔았는데, 놀랍도록 쉬웠고 약 150,000원(약 110달러)을 받았습니다. 이 플랫폼들은 편리하고, 종종 지역적이며(동네에서 판매자와 만날 수 있습니다), 다른 곳에서는 볼 수 없는 것을 찾을 수 있기 때문에 엄청나게 인기가 많습니다. 돈을 절약하고, 친환경적이며, 여전히 스타일리시하거나 원하는 기기를 얻을 수 있는 현명한 방법입니다.

> 요점: 온라인 리셀 플랫폼은 이제 편리함과 가치에 힘입어 독특한 아이템을 찾고 지속 가능한 쇼핑을 수용하기 위한 필수적인 수단입니다.

Seoul is famous for its bustling cafes, but what is hot in Seoul this week isn't just about the prettiest latte art anymore. People, especially after a long week of work and the constant palli-palli (hurry-hurry) culture, are actively seeking out 'healing' spaces. These aren't necessarily quiet, meditative places, but rather cafes with a unique, often retro or nature-inspired theme that encourages slower living. Think LP (long-play record) listening cafes in Euljiro where you can actually pick out vinyl, or plant-filled greenhouses that serve as coffee shops in Ikseon-dong. My girlfriend dragged me to one of these 'forest-themed' cafes last weekend, tucked away in a tiny alley near Anguk Station. It was packed, but the vibe was so different – soft jazz, dim lighting, and everyone just quietly enjoying their drinks or reading. It's about finding these hidden gems in niche neighborhoods that haven't been fully gentrified or overrun by tourists yet. Using Naver Maps or Kakao Maps to scout out these specific, often tiny, spots is part of the adventure. It’s a rebellion against the mainstream, a search for authentic experiences where you can genuinely relax, even for an hour or two.

> Point: Locals are trading flashy, Instagrammable spots for genuinely calming, uniquely themed 'healing' cafes in less explored parts of the city.

## K-Resale Culture: Secondhand is the New New

Sustainability and unique finds are big right now, and the K-resale market is absolutely exploding. What is hot in Seoul this week in fashion and home goods is increasingly about finding pre-owned treasures. It's not just about vintage shops in Gwangjang Market anymore. It's largely driven by apps like 'Karrot Market' (당근마켓, Danggeun Market) or 'Bunjang' (번개장터, Bungae Jangteo), where people buy and sell everything from luxury handbags and limited-edition sneakers to used electronics and even furniture. My younger sister is obsessed with finding unique clothing pieces on these apps. She claims she snagged a nearly-new designer bag for half price last month. I actually sold an old gaming console on Karrot Market recently; it was surprisingly easy, and I got about ₩150,000 (around $110 USD) for it. These platforms are incredibly popular because they're convenient, often local (you can meet up with sellers in your neighborhood), and you can find things you won't see anywhere else. It’s a savvy way to save money, be eco-conscious, and still stay stylish or get the gadgets you want.

> Point: Online resale platforms are now a go-to for finding unique items and embracing sustainable shopping, driven by convenience and value.
